rounds.text: Shilp Gravures Ltd is trading at a heavily discounted valuation of 10.1x P/E, sitting at just 0.81x book value with a share price of ₹ 139 against a book value of ₹ 171 [E1, E2]. This undervaluation is further highlighted by a favorable comparison to sector benchmarks, where the company trades at a P/E of 13.21x and a P/B of 0.84x against sector benchmarks of 22.51x and 2.4x respectively [E6, E7]. Operationally, the business is showing improvement with its TTM operating margin expanding to 15%, representing a one percentage point increase from three years earlier [E29]. Shareholders are also being rewarded with a positive dividend yield of 1.51% while the market capitalization stands at ₹ 85.9 Cr [E3, E4]. Conceded: the company faces profitability headwinds with a low median return on equity of 6% over 5 years and 5% over 3 years, alongside an ROA of 5.53% that trails the sector benchmark of 6.46% [E8, E26, E27].

Conceded: [E1], [E2], [E6], [E7], [E9], and [E29]. Despite these apparent low valuation multiples and modest margin improvements, the fundamental profitability of Shilp Gravures Ltd is persistently depressed [E57]. The company's median return on equity over a 3-year period is a meager 5%, and over a 5-year period it languishes at 6% [E26, E27]. Filed statements explicitly flag this low return on equity as a negative, noting a 4.87% figure over the last three years [E57]. Furthermore, the return on assets sits below the sector benchmark at 5.53% [E8], while recent quarterly operating margins have contracted by 1 percentage point compared to the year-ago period [E30]. Reflecting these underlying operational weaknesses, the stock sits merely 6% of the way up its 52-week range [E5].

Conceded: [E57]. The bear relies heavily on historical median returns on equity of 5% to 6% [E26, E27] and low past figures [E57], but this backward-looking pessimism completely ignores the recent momentum where ROE has recovered to 8.41% and the current trailing twelve month operating margin has expanded to 15% from 13% three years prior [E9, E29]. While the bear points to a sector ROA deficit [E8], it fails to acknowledge that the company's P/E of 10.1x to 13.21x and P/B of 0.81x to 0.84x trade at a massive, unwarranted discount to sector benchmarks of 22.51x and 2.4x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7].

Conceded: [E29]. The bull celebrates a modest margin expansion to 15% [E29], yet the most recent quarterly data reveals that operating margins have already slipped to 14% in June 2026 compared to 15% in the year-ago quarter [E30]. The bull dismisses historical returns, but a multi-year trend cannot be brushed aside when the median return on equity sat at a meager 5% over 3 years and 6% over 5 years [E26, E27], formally flagged as a low return of 4.87% [E57]. Furthermore, the bull’s reliance on discounted multiples ignores the operational reality that the company generates a return on assets of only 5.53% against the sector benchmark of 6.46% [E8]. This persistent underperformance in core capital efficiency justifies the lower valuation rather than making it a mispriced bargain, especially as the stock languishes at just 6% of its 52-week range [E5].
